meta.description: Pretrain a fresh KERMT model from scratch on a user-provided corpus. Builds a new vocabulary from the corpus, instantiates the model architecture from defaults, and launches pretrain_ddp.py inside the kermt container (detached for long runs). Unlike kermt-continue-pretrain, no starting checkpoint is loaded — the model is randomly initialized.

recommendations.title: Add decision tree for pretrain-target-mode selection
recommendations.problem: Modes described (vocab=lightweight, hybrid=SOTA, cmim=contrastive) but no guidance on when to choose each for specific use cases
recommendations.root_cause: Assumes user understands tradeoffs between modes from brief descriptions
recommendations.fix: Add to Inputs section after mode descriptions: 'Choosing a mode: Use vocab for fast lightweight pretraining when downstream tasks don't need contrastive features; use cmim for pure contrastive learning; use hybrid (recommended) for best downstream performance combining both objectives, at cost of slightly longer training.'

recommendations.title: Reference shared hardware requirements instead of duplicating
recommendations.problem: Hardware requirements table fully duplicated from kermt-continue-pretrain including GPU indexing caveat
recommendations.root_cause: Copy-paste for self-containment increases maintenance burden
recommendations.fix: Replace Hardware requirements section with: 'Same as kermt-continue-pretrain (see that skill for GPU/VRAM/disk details). Key difference: Wall time is days-scale for from-scratch pretraining vs hours for continue-pretrain, even on multi-GPU. The skill estimates runtime before launch.'

recommendations.title: Add guidance for large corpus vocab building failures
recommendations.problem: No handling documented for scenarios where vocabulary building fails or runs out of memory on very large corpora (tens of millions of molecules)
recommendations.root_cause: Assumes prepare_data vocab building always succeeds
recommendations.fix: Add to Common errors: 'prepare_data vocab building OOM or timeout → very large corpora (>50M molecules) may need chunked vocab building. Consider sampling a representative subset for vocab construction, then using full corpus for training with --vocab-dir pointing to pre-built vocab.'

recommendations.title: Add idempotency statement for repeated from-scratch runs
recommendations.problem: No explicit guidance on whether running from-scratch multiple times with same corpus produces similar models
recommendations.root_cause: Random initialization and stochastic training not discussed
recommendations.fix: Add to Hard rules: 'Idempotency: from-scratch pretraining with same corpus and --seed N produces deterministic data splits and shuffling, but model initialization is random. Different runs will converge to different local minima. For reproducible research, save and version final checkpoints rather than regenerating.'
